_comment: THE CANONICAL unanswerable-existence CASES, read by BOTH modules' tests.
oasgen-provider decides this at generation time (restdefinition.unanswerableExistence) and warns
on the RestDefinition, so somebody can add a findby while the document is still being written.
rest-dynamic-controller decides the same thing at runtime and returns
unstructured-runtime's ErrExistenceUnanswerable, so the runtime stops and reports instead of
stranding the CR. They cannot share code -- separate Go modules, no dependency either way, and
both predicates live under internal/ -- so they share THIS FILE instead.
That is the enforceable version of 'one predicate'. A comment saying 'keep these in sync' is not:
it fails silently, and the whole point is that a WARNING and a RUNTIME REFUSAL must not disagree
about which kinds they describe. If the two drift, a row here fails in the other module's suite.
WHY THE PREDICATE IS WHAT IT IS. The runtime's existence check picks its read verb by
ADDRESSABILITY, not by which verbs exist: it dry-runs the GET, and only when that does not
validate does it fall back to findby. A get parameter sourced from status is empty at reconcile 1,
so the GET does not validate, the action becomes findby, and if none is declared the check can
NEVER answer -- because the only thing that would fill that status field is the create response
that was lost. Measured: 4 of 6 CRs in one consumer's chart stranded on a CLEAN install, 2 more on
another consumer's chart. See unstructured-runtime issue 119.
DELIBERATELY NARROW. A parameter with NO mapping is not flagged: it may still resolve by name from
the generated spec, and deciding that here would mean re-deriving the rendered schema in both
modules -- an approximation of the real resolver, which is how a vacuous gate got written in this
repo. A false negative is possible; a false positive is not. Measured on one consumer's chart: ten
findby-less kinds split SIX exposed and FOUR not, and warning on all ten would have sent operators
to do manual work on four kinds that need none.

specFields is the set of top-level spec property names of the GENERATED kind. A get path parameter whose NAME appears there resolves from the spec even when its status source is empty, so it must NOT be flagged. An EMPTY specFields means 'none', not 'unknown'.

cases.name: the measured case: get needs a status id, no findby
a declared findby makes it answerable, whatever the get needs
get addresses from spec, so it validates at reconcile 1
no get verb at all is a DIFFERENT defect, reported elsewhere
an unmapped parameter is NOT flagged -- it may resolve by name from the spec
one of three parameters comes from status -- one is enough
action casing does not matter for get
action casing does not matter for findby either
the DEPRECATED mapping field is read too, or pre-rename definitions go unwarned
a status-mapped param that ALSO resolves from the spec is answerable (github Repository)
cases.why: builder.go fills path parameters from spec BY NAME (processFields at 179) BEFORE applying explicit mappings (236), and a mapping whose source is absent hits `continue` (27-29). So with status.name empty the parameter keeps spec.name, IsResourceKnown's dry-run GET succeeds, and the existence check never falls through to findby. Measured by github-provider-kog: a pre-create GET addresses spec.name and 404s, then status.name takes over after the create (their issue 386).

cases.name: the SAME shape with the param excluded from the spec is still unanswerable (github Team)
cases.why: team_slug is NOT a spec property, so there is no by-name fallback at processFields and the parameter really is empty at reconcile 1. The negative twin of the Repository case: same mapping shape, opposite verdict, decided ONLY by the spec-field set -- so a predicate ignoring specFields would pass this case and fail the one above.
